resources.string: Scan a truck, shoot its 360, walk away. Uploads finish in the background.
How this works in the field
Waiting for internet — you\'re on the GoPro\'s Wi-Fi. Turn Wi-Fi off to upload over cellular, or join a network with internet.
Waiting for internet. Photos are saved and will upload on their own once you\'re back online.

Photos are saved to this device the moment they\'re taken. Uploading happens by itself in the background — you never have to wait for it, and nothing is lost if you walk away, close the app, or lose signal.
Turn the camera on and connect this device to the GoPro\'s own Wi-Fi network. That network has no internet, which is normal and expected.

Scan a truck\'s QR code, check the truck number on screen matches the sticker, then capture. Shoot as many angles as you need, tap Done, and move to the next truck. Stay on the GoPro\'s Wi-Fi the whole time.
If this device has cellular data, photos upload as you go — no action needed. If it doesn\'t, they queue up and wait. Twenty or more trucks in the queue is fine.
If anything is still waiting, turn Wi-Fi off so cellular takes over, or join a Wi-Fi network that has internet. The queue empties on its own. You can close the app — it keeps going.
The Uploads screen lists every photo and its status, and the diagnostics log at the bottom records each scan and capture step. A photo that says PENDING is safe — it just hasn\'t found internet yet.
Every capture is written twice: a working copy that is deleted once it uploads, and your own copy in Documents/TruckCapture, which stays on the device either way.
Use this only when the QR code won\'t scan. Photos taken this way have no GUID and are filed under the truck number alone.
Point the camera at the truck\'s QR code
Camera permission is needed to scan truck codes.
Upload is running in the background. You can keep shooting or move on.
